when_to_use: riff-driven jazz-funk or fusion where pressure accumulates through layering and releases through a decisive breakdown-and-return, 96-124 BPM

defaults.feel: tight 16th funk, hard backbeat, locked to the riff

signature_moves: static vamp: hold one dominant or sus field while bass and drums make the riff feel increasingly inevitable
modal interchange stab: Em9 -> Ebmaj7#11 -> Em9, used as a sudden flash of friction that disappears before it becomes a new progression
sus-to-dom release: Gsus13 -> G13 at the section's arrival, turning suspended pressure into a clean collective hit
quartal upper-structure over a pedal bass, adding width and altitude without distracting from the groove
cadence_options: vamp turnaround: Em9 -> A13 -> back to the riff, keeping momentum circular rather than conclusive
breakdown then release: strip to bass riff, let the absence create tension, then let the full band reclaim beat 1 together
no functional cadence when the strongest release is the return of weight, register, and ensemble unity
avoid: letting harmony wander; here harmony must sharpen the riff rather than compete with it (see style-cheatsheets Jazz-funk/fusion)
a laid-back drag; this pocket is assertive and on the grid, not borrowed from neo-soul (see ../references/cliche-register.md)

hook_archetypes.name: locked-jaw-riff
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a syncopated 16th riff struck by bass and lead or keys in unison, with one rest that makes the next downbeat feel unavoidable
hook_archetypes.contour: an angular gesture around root and b7 that snaps back to the root on beat 1 like a mechanical latch
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Intro, bass alone first, then the band joins so the same riff suddenly carries collective force

hook_archetypes.name: flash-stab
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a full-band off-beat accent that interrupts the vamp for a fraction of a bar and leaves the groove intact afterward
hook_archetypes.contour: an upper-structure chord hit such as Ebmaj7#11 over E, heard as a bright fracture rather than a modulation
hook_archetypes.first_appears: the first build, marking the moment the vamp stops feeling contained

urgency.note_lengths: short, driving, and riff-locked; rests should sharpen repetition rather than soften it
urgency.contour: angular and tight around root and b7, with insistence created by exact return points
urgency.placement: on the grid, forward and uncompromising

build.note_lengths: phrases lengthen only as register rises; avoid adding notes that do not increase pressure
build.contour: reach higher on each pass while the harmony remains static, making the same ground feel less stable
build.placement: on the grid, pushing toward a collective event

peak.note_lengths: choose one held high target or a concise screaming figure over the fullest vamp rather than continuous display
peak.contour: sustain the top tension tone while ensemble hits define the edges of the phrase

release.note_lengths: open the phrasing after the breakdown; fewer notes should feel larger because the band has just returned
release.contour: resolve downward toward the root and let the riff regain its original shape
release.placement: on the grid, relaxing the push without losing precision

drum_skeleton.low_energy: kick locks to the bass riff, hard snare sits on 2 and 4, and steady 16th hats make the vamp feel engineered but human
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: increase kick dialogue with the riff, add ghost snares between backbeats, and open the hat only where the arrangement needs another edge
drum_skeleton.high_energy: drive full 16ths, reinforce ensemble stabs, then remove most of the kit for the breakdown so the re-entry carries physical weight

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: bass states the proposition alone; drums turn it into a contract; keys widen the field; lead gives the pressure a face. Build by adding layers that agree on the riff, not by multiplying unrelated ideas. At the breakdown, strip to the bass riff long enough for the listener to feel the missing mass. Re-enter the full band on one unmistakable downbeat.

anti_boredom_rules: the vamp must visibly accumulate and shed pressure; one static texture across the whole piece is a structural failure
include at least one breakdown followed by a full-band return whose impact comes from prior subtraction
the riff hook must recur with a change of register, layering, orchestration, rest placement, or upper-structure color
ghost figures and primary riff accents must remain dynamically and texturally distinct so the groove has hierarchy
harmony stays subservient to groove, but at least one signature_move must create a memorable fracture or release

bass_behavior.role: primary unison riff and harmonic anchor
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: tightly doubles kick and selected lead attacks
bass_behavior.density: continuous syncopated riff with breakdown exposure

groove_intent.hihat: steady straight sixteenths with accent openings
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: bass, drums, and lead converge on unison riffs and release hits

distinguishing_traits: tight on-grid funk instead of laid-back push-pull
dynamic breakdown and abrupt full-band release define the arc
